text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `latency.p99 > 2.5s` for `inference.prod.us-east-1` (10m window). Auto-page to #eng-oncall.

pagerduty: PD Incident INC-2026-9876 created and routed to eng-oncall. Priority: P1.

mira: acked. I’m on it — grabbing metrics and recent deploys.

alex: thx mira. I’m pulling traces now. Any customer-facing symptoms reported?

sam: support says a couple of customers see timeouts on generation endpoints. Low % but high-value.

jordan: seeing a sudden jump in tail tokens served per request and KV cache eviction spike in the last ~8m. Could be cache thrash after the canary.

mira: timeline: 07:14 UTC canary rollout of `model-v2-quant` started, steady for 5m, 07:20 we start seeing p95 climb, 07:24 p99 spikes. Canary traffic was ~8-10%.

alex: graphs: `kvcache.evictions/sec` up x6, `gpu_util` normal, but `latency.p99` correlated with `kvcache.miss.latency`.

sam: suspect: new model variant changed request token patterns causing larger KV footprint -> eviction churn.

jordan: also seeing many small requests with long contexts from a single client IP — not respecting prefix caching.

incident-bot: Suggested runbook: 1) Pause canary rollout 2) Fail traffic back to `model-v2-fp16` 3) Increase KV cache size on warm nodes 4) Engage Platform to scale dedicated pool.

mira: paused the canary in CI/CD at 07:26 UTC (command: `deployctl pause --canary model-v2-quant`).

alex: rolling back canary traffic -> routing change in progress. Command: ```sh
kubectl apply -f routing/production/route-backfill.yaml
# sets traffic: model-v2-fp16=100%
```

jordan: routing change applied at 07:28 UTC. Watchdogs show traffic moved off `model-v2-quant`.

sam: contacting Platform to bump `kvcache.size` on the warm pool nodes. Pinged @platform on their channel.

platform (via incident-bot): scaling warm pool +1 replica, increasing cache config on the replica. ETA ~3m.

mira: p95 is dropping slowly, p99 still elevated but trending down from 3.8s -> 2.1s.

pagerduty: INC-2026-9876 acknowledged by mira at 07:27 UTC. Escalation policy paused.

alex: from traces: closure time includes repeated KV lookups for same prefix across sharded KV; some requests serialized waiting on lock. Could be lock contention in cache backend.

jordan: logs show `kvcache.lock-time` spikes to 120ms on a couple nodes. Not universal. Maybe a GC or background compaction kicked in.

mira: mitigations applied: routing rollback + warm-pool scale. Requesting a temporary config change: `kvcache.eviction_threshold=0.85 -> 0.95` to avoid aggressive evictions.

sam: Platform applied `eviction_threshold=0.95` on warm pool at 07:31 UTC. Confirmed.

mira: p99 now 1.4s. Customer errors dropping. Support notified customers A and B of transient latency with note we are mitigating.

alex: next steps: 1) full rollback of `model-v2-quant` until we root-cause token footprint change, 2) run storage/compaction analysis on cache nodes, 3) adapt canary config to smaller traffic step and warm-cache priming prior to rollout.

jordan: I’ll take the root-cause on kvcache compaction/locks. Will collect heap/gc stats and open an infra ticket.

sam: I’ll document a short playbook for future model canaries: pre-warm keys, start with 1% traffic, monitor `kvcache.evictions/sec` and `lock-time` -> auto-abort on threshold.

mira: agree. Also propose adding a quick fallback variant with quantized model but same request footprint (test harness).

pagerduty: INC-2026-9876 status update: Root cause suspected: canary model variant increased KV footprint causing eviction churn and lock contention in cache layer.

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2 at 07:35 UTC after p99 stabilized < 1.5s and customer impact limited.

mira: handing off to jordan for post-incident RCA. I’ll stay on standby for rollback followups.

jordan: acknowledged handoff. Will lead RCA and postmortem. ETA doc in 24h.

sam: action items (quick):
- [ ] Jordan: collect kvcache heap/gc + compaction timeline (owner)
- [ ] Platform: add warm-pool pre-warm disk/keys and 1 replica buffer
- [ ] DevEx: update canary runbook with priming + 1% traffic start
- [ ] Support: confirm which customers saw errors & share correspondence

mira: closing notes: nice quick response everyone. Two immediate wins: rollback + warm pool scale prevented broader impact. Postmortem draft please include measurable thresholds for auto-abort.

alex: thanks. I’ll schedule a follow-up sync with Platform and Model Onboarding to adjust rollout gating.

pagerduty: INC-2026-9876 resolved at 07:42 UTC (no open alerts).

incident-bot: Incident thread closed; link to postmortem to be added by jordan. :white_check_mark:
